summary: Philip Airport (PHP/KPHP) is a small public-use general aviation airport serving the city of Philip in Haakon County, South Dakota. It supports local air travel for the rural community and surrounding ranching region in the west-central part of the state. The airport features a single runway and primarily handles private, charter, and light recreational aircraft.
faqs:
Q: Does Philip Airport offer commercial airline service?
A: No, Philip Airport is a general aviation facility with no scheduled commercial flights. Travelers typically use nearby regional airports for commercial service.

Q: How many runways does Philip Airport have?
A: The airport has one runway suitable for small to mid-sized general aviation aircraft.

Q: Are there fueling services available at the airport?
A: Fuel availability can vary; pilots should contact the airport or Fixed-Base Operator in advance to confirm current services and hours.

Q: Is the airport open to public use?
A: Yes, Philip Airport is a public-use airport, though it has limited staffing and is primarily unattended outside of arranged visits.
transport_tips: There is no public transit service to Philip Airport, so arriving travelers will need to arrange ground transportation in advance. Rental cars may be available from agencies in the town of Philip or larger nearby cities. Having a personal vehicle is the most practical option for getting to and from the airport.
local_tip: While in Philip, visit the Pioneer Auto Show, a renowned collection of over 250 antique cars and motorcycles, which is one of the most popular attractions in this part of South Dakota.
